_about: LINES OF FIRE, STAGE 1 (decision line-of-fire, builder LOF1, 2026-10-11): the height grid and the line check (scripts/sim/height_grid.gd, height_grid_build.gd, line_of_fire.gd, line_of_fire_shapes.gd read this through scripts/sim/line_of_fire_rules.gd). ALEX'S (decision line-of-fire, option b): real lines of fire against every blocker's height; trees THIN (a chance per canopy to stop a round); hull-down with TWO layers, hull and turret; a target that is fully hidden is HELD ('otherwise we would just mow down anything in between on purpose'); the same line check between planes and the ground (hills can block the low band). THE METHOD (agreed): 2.5D. A straight line is walked across a grid of top heights; nothing is a 3D mesh. EVERYTHING BELOW IS PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (cell size, block size, tree band, tree chance, sample counts): none is Alex's. STAGE 2 (builder LOF2, 2026-10-12; Alex: 'proceed with stage 2') HOOKED COMBAT TO IT behind 'enabled' (false: play does not change until Alex has looked at the proofs): see the 'odds' and 'targets' sections, scripts/sim/combat_lines.gd, line_of_fire_odds.gd and the resolver's use_lines branch. Record shape as data/sim/bombs.json: {value, _proposed, _reason}. Metres.

enabled._reason: The switch of stage 2: false, so combat is exactly what it was (byte for byte: the same events from eight seeded runs before and after the hook). With true, SandboxScenario.populate gives the World the lines of fire (World.set_line_of_fire): straight rounds (the weapons in odds.weapons) need a line to the target and take their odds from the visible share. Alex flips it once he has looked at the proofs (tmp/lof2/)

cell_m._reason: A cell is 1 m square. Chosen by measurement on the Strike (seed 20261009) and Hold the bridge (seed 55), the whole 5 km map, one thread, the machine busy: at 1 m 92 to 94 MB (277 to 283 of the 400 chunks hold arrays, the rest are one height), cells 22 to 24 s plus 13 to 14 s of the map's trees; at 2 m 24 MB, cells 8 to 9 s plus the same trees. A check costs the same at both (20 to 30 us). 1 m is taken because the sandbag ring is 1 m thick and a 2 m cell would make it 2 m, and a wall can be 1.35 m; Alex: RAM is not the worry (decision memory-budget). 2 m is the one-value switch (a coarser ring, a third of the cell time, a quarter of the memory). Must divide the terrain chunk (256 m) and be a whole number of blocks

block_m._reason: The coarse step of the line walk: the grid keeps the highest top of every 16 m block, and a line that passes above a whole block skips it without looking at its cells. Measured on the village and its woods: a tank-high 300 m line walks about 10 blocks and 11 cells (it is stopped early), a 350 m plane line about 22 blocks and 4 cells, a plane over the village 25 blocks and none; without the blocks a 350 m line is about 500 cells. Must be a whole number of cells and divide the chunk

materials._reason: The cell kinds, by id, each named in THE ONE VOCABULARY for what a round hits (data/sim/rounds.json vocabulary.materials: metal, stone, wood, earth, water; builder G3, 2026-10-12, so the grid, a unit's boxes and a unit's material say the same words; this renamed ground to earth, timber to wood, earthworks to earth, and merged armour, aircraft and ship into metal). Two kinds can share a name because they differ in what they are, not in what a round hits: id 0 is open ground (earth) and id 4 the sandbags and earthworks (raised earth: a vehicle is driven over open ground and stands on top of it, but it stands UNDER a sandbag cell), id 3 a house (wood) and id 5 a tree's canopy (wood, never a cell). Ids: 0 open ground, 1 water, 2 stone (walls, the bridge), 3 house, 4 raised earth, 5 canopy, 6 metal (a unit box only; no cell is metal). The code fixes the first six and checks them on load; the names must be in the vocabulary. `material_id(name)` is the first id of a name (earth is 0, wood is 3); a STAMPED box of earth puts id 4 in the grid (rules.stamp_id)

wall_material._reason: the village's walls (the compound's ring and divider) are stone (the damage-looks table: stone = the bridge, walls)

house_material._reason: the village's houses are wood (the damage-looks table: timber = houses; renamed to the round model's word, data/sim/rounds.json)

scenery._heights_from: NOT A TUNABLE, A NOTE: a wall's and a house's height is the structure's own `h` (scripts/world/structures.gd sync_struct: wall_height, and house_size x house_height_ratio, in map px) divided by the map scale, and a tree's is the tree's own `h` (scene_gen.gd sync_tree, scaled and held to the tree height window) over the scale. Decision scenery-heights (Alex: 'S1 real heights') is live in those lines (2026-10-12): houses about 6 to 8 m, the compound's walls 1.1 to 2.5 m, trees 8 to 20 m, and it flowed into the grid with no change here (test_scenery_heights holds it)

margin_m._reason: How far from a shore (in the water's own depth units, metres of water) an 8 m lattice cell is taken as wholly wet or wholly dry from its five samples; a cell nearer than this to a shore is decided cell by cell with the sim's own water query (WaterGen.depth_at). Checked against that query in test_line_of_fire

base_frac._reason: Where a canopy's band starts, as a fraction of the tree's height above its ground. 0: a tree stops a low line from the ground up (trunk, branches and crown as a low gun sees them), so rounds hit trees (Alex's own question, 'cross over sandbags but hit tanks, or houses, or maybe even trees'). A raised crown (0.3) would let a tank's round pass under every tree

stop_chance._reason: Alex: trees are THIN, 'a chance per canopy to stop a round'. The chance that a line through the middle of a canopy (a full-diameter chord) is stopped; the number is the lead's guess, a dial. A grove of five canopies in a row passes a line with 0.65^5 = 12 percent

scale_by_chord._reason: true: the chance is stop_chance x (the line's chord through the canopy's band over the canopy's diameter), so a line that only grazes a crown is rarely stopped; false: stop_chance flat per canopy, Alex's words read literally

roll_salt._reason: mixed into every canopy roll. The roll is a hash of (this salt, the caller's roll key, the canopy's id): its own stream, never the combat stream (combat seeds every roll from a unit's index; scripts/sim/combat.gd roll_seed), so asking where a line stops never shifts the dice. The same key and the same line always give the same answer on every peer

row_spacing_m._reason: STAGE 2 (builder LOF2): the rows of a box are about this far apart, SPREAD from just under its top to just over its bottom (row_edge_inset_m), so the top band is always looked at. Stage 1 put them at the middle of equal slices (0.5 m: a hull 1.5 m high got rows at 0.25, 0.75 and 1.25), and its finding was that a 1.35 m wall hid every row of a 1.5 m hull. Now a hull 1.5 m high gets 6 rows (0.05 to 1.45 m), a turret 0.8 m gets 4, and a row's WEIGHT is the band it stands for (the trapezoid rule), so a wall at 1.35 m leaves the top row and its 0.1 of the hull in view. Cost: a tank seen broadside is about 40 lines, an exposure about 1 ms

col_spacing_m._reason: and in columns this far apart across the silhouette (a 3 m wide hull gets 3 columns), each at the middle of its slice

max_rows._reason: at most this many rows per box, so a 25 m tall radio tower or a bomber is not 60 lines (was 3 in stage 1, when the rows were equal slices)

row_edge_inset_m._reason: STAGE 2 (builder LOF2): the first and the last row of a box stand this far inside its bottom and its top: a row exactly at the bottom would be a line into the ground the box stands on, and one exactly at the top a line along the edge of a wall of the same height

max_cols._reason: at most this many columns per box. A tank seen end on is 3 rows x 4 columns for the hull and 2 x 3 for the turret, 18 lines; a bomber 5 x 3 = 15

not_targets._reason: STAGE 2 (builder LOF2): the parts of a unit that are never aimed at: the low bridge's deck (a level surface at the banks' height, with no side to hit; the parapets are the bridge as a target). A part is named here, not marked in each unit's file, so no unit file needs a new field

odds._about: STAGE 2 (builder LOF2, decision line-of-fire, 'proceed with stage 2'; Alex on tank accuracy: 'yes but directly impacts 9'). THE MODEL, PROPOSED: for a STRAIGHT round (bullets and cannon: a weapon named in 'weapons' below; the arcs and the air bursts keep their old rules) the chance of a hit per roll is the SHARE OF THE ROUND'S SPREAD THAT FALLS ON THE TARGET'S VISIBLE PARTS. The spread is a two-dimensional normal distribution about the aim point, in the plane across the line of fire, with a standard deviation of (the weapon's angular spread) x (the distance): s = spread_mrad / 1000 x metres. The target's silhouette is cut into the cells the sample lines are traced to (columns across, rows up each box, hull and turret apart); a cell is VISIBLE if its line reaches it (nothing in the height grid, no tree that rolled to stop it); the chance is the sum, over the visible cells, of the share of the normal curve that falls in the cell. Range and size come out of it: a far or small target takes a smaller share of the curve (decision tank-accuracy: accuracy falls with range and rises with the target's size), a tank behind a wall shows only its turret and takes the share on the turret, and a target with NO visible cell is HELD (not fired on: Alex, 'Hold, otherwise we would just mow down anything in between on purpose'). THE OLD FACTORS: base_hit_chance is replaced by this share for these weapons (it stays the calibration: each spread is set so that a still, fully exposed target at the weapon's typical range, seen from every side, takes the weapon's old base_hit_chance); the centre (aim quality in the cone), range (the fringe past the effective range) and crossing_rate (the target's motion) factors stay, multiplied on. A weapon not in 'weapons' (flak) is unchanged. Alex's words and decisions are in decisions.json (line-of-fire, tank-accuracy); every number below is PROPOSED.

aim._reason: Where the gunner aims on the target: the centroid of the parts he can see (a tank behind a wall is aimed at by its turret, and the rounds that fall short land in the wall). The other setting, silhouette_centre, aims at the middle of the whole target as the old model did (a hull-down tank is then hit much less)

landing_attempts._reason: A round that MISSED is drawn from its own spread again and again until the draw falls outside the visible parts (rejection sampling, bounded: the loop is never open). At most this many draws; a spread wholly inside the visible parts (close range) would otherwise take for ever, and then the round is placed just outside the silhouette

miss_run_m._reason: A round that missed flies on from the point where it passed the target and is followed this far, to the first thing it meets (a cell's top, a canopy, the ground or the water). If it meets nothing in that run (a round aimed up at a plane) it is reported as lost in the air at the end of the run

landing_salt._reason: Mixed into the seed of the stream a round's landing is drawn from. The stream is the roll's own (the combat seed of that hardpoint, that tick and that roll, through this salt): NO number is ever drawn from the combat dice for it (CLAUDE.md: combat seeds every roll from the shooter's index, so an extra draw would reshuffle every later roll)

roll_key_salt._reason: Mixed into the key the trees' rolls on one shot's lines are made from (scripts/sim/line_of_fire.gd canopy_roll), so that the same canopy is not stopped by the same dice in every shot

weapons._about: The straight rounds: every weapon whose round has the path 'straight' in data/sim/rounds.json (bullets and cannon rounds) is listed here, and no other (test_line_of_fire_combat holds both). spread_mrad: the angular spread (the standard deviation, milliradians) of the round about the aim, SET BY scripts/test_support/lof_calibrate.gd so that the reference case, a still, fully exposed target of the named type at the typical range, seen from eight sides (every 45 degrees) and at the elevation given, takes the old base_hit_chance (reference.odds, held equal to the weapon's own by the test). The typical ranges are PROPOSED (the lead's reading of how each weapon is used; Alex said the tank gun's is about 200 m).
